## Empirical anchor

The R1-R4 spec-audit cadence (2026-05-17) produced N=4 empirical data points on the substrate principle that "structural fixes succeed where procedural fixes recur" (per §4.6 TIRO + §27 mechanical-script / agent-inspection split + the §12 structural rewrite). The actual pattern across R1 → R4 is more nuanced than the original framing implied:

**Finding-count convergence:** R1 (49 findings) → R2 (5 new) → R3 (2 new) → R4 (1 new). Iteration produces diminishing returns; the audit cadence converges; spec quality improves at each pass.

**Drift surface evolution:**

| Pass | Drift surface | Location |
|---|---|---|
| Pre-R2 | Huge | §12.1-§12.5 full snapshots |
| Post-R2 fold-in | Small | §12.3 + §12.5 single enumeration sentence |
| Post-R3 fold-in | Same size | §13.10 bullet 4 single enumeration sentence (relocated) |
| Post-R4 (accepted option (b)) | Same size, soft-residue | §13.10 bullet 4 with known-residue parenthetical |

The drift surface SHRANK substantially from R1 → R2 → R3 (full snapshots → single enumeration). It DID NOT shrink between R3 → R4 fold-ins; the location MOVED (§12 → §13.10). The relocation is operationally softer (§13.10's job is to be updated; §12 should never drift) but the structural drift class is not zero.

## The refined principle (candidate for future canonification)

Original framing implied by Arc 33 §27 + Arc 38 candidate stoa--ojz §4.6 TIRO + the §12 structural rewrite:

> **"Structural fixes succeed where procedural fixes recur."**

R4-supported refinement:

> **"Structural fixes succeed at narrowing the drift surface; full closure requires propagation discipline applied at fix-author time AND iteration to catch propagation gaps the fix-author missed. Each fold-in iteration that catches propagation gaps shrinks the drift surface further but may not fully eliminate the class — the residual converges on a fixed-point that is operationally acceptable rather than structurally zero."**

Two halves both matter:
1. Structural fixes ARE meaningfully better than procedural fixes (R1 → R4 confirms the drift surface shrunk by an order of magnitude across iterations).
2. Propagation discipline at fix-author time is load-bearing (R3 caught what R2's fix missed; R4 caught what R3's fix missed).

## Why N=4 doesn't yet justify substrate-canon promotion

Per `operating-disciplines.md` §6.7.1 N=1 honesty discipline: substrate-canon promotion requires multi-class-evidence + controlled comparison + substrate-level pattern. N=4 across consecutive iterations on a single drift class (the §12/§13 staleness pattern) is repeated-instance evidence, not multi-class evidence.

The principle refinement is *suggestive* across multiple substrate-domains:
- §4.6 TIRO bw specialist (Arc 38 candidate; not yet built; will test the refined principle when shipped)
- §27 mechanical-script / agent-inspection split (Arc 33 shipped; observable across multiple arcs since)
- §12 structural rewrite (R2/R3/R4 fold-ins; the empirical anchor for this ticket)

A genuinely multi-class test would require:
- A 4th structural-fix arc on a different substrate-domain
- Comparison against a parallel arc that applied a procedural fix
- Multi-arc observation over several months to test the asymptote prediction

This ticket files the empirical anchor + the candidate refinement so future structural-fix arcs can accrete evidence + eventually canonify the refined principle if the pattern holds.

## Two empirical predictions worth tracking

R4's closing observation surfaced two falsifiable predictions:

1. **If a hypothetical R5 fold-in adopts NC8 option (a) — rewrite §13.10 bullet 4 to dynamic-walk language — does an R5 audit find another latent surface elsewhere?** If yes, asymptote is at "one residual enumeration somewhere; location moves but count holds." If no, iteration genuinely converges to zero.

2. **If PRINCIPAL accepts option (b) — leave §13.10 bullet 4 as-is — does the enumeration actually drift in practice over 3-6 months?** Over the next several arcs as new §13.x sections potentially get added, does the bullet stay current via Pass 8 reconciliation, or does it accumulate stale enumerations?

PRINCIPAL accepted option (b) on 2026-05-17. Prediction 2 is now live; data accretes over time. Prediction 1 remains hypothetical (would require a future iteration on a similar structural fix).

## Substrate touch-point (if/when canonified)

Likely insertion: `operating-disciplines.md` new section sibling to §27 (mechanical-script / agent-inspection split). Candidate title: "Structural fixes converge to a fixed-point, not zero — propagation discipline at fix-author time is load-bearing." Body articulates the principle + cites the §12 staleness pattern's R1-R4 cadence as the originating empirical anchor + cross-refs §4.6 TIRO + §27 + future structural-fix arcs as N-accretion sites.

## Gauntlet (if/when arc-shipped)

DAEDALUS + ARGUS + ADA + CATO. Substrate-prose-only edit. ~50-80 LOC for the new canon section. Small arc.

## Sequencing

P4 ACCRETION. Not load-bearing for spec-met (the spec already operates correctly under the original framing). Accretes evidence over multiple future structural-fix arcs. Promote to canon when N≥3 multi-class data points support the refined principle.

## Cross-refs

- SPEC_AUDIT.md (R1) — first observation of the §12 staleness pattern
- SPEC_AUDIT_R2.md — R2 recurrence + structural fix recommendation
- SPEC_AUDIT_R3.md — R3 verdict "still latent" after first structural fix
- SPEC_AUDIT_R4.md — R4 verdict "fully closed at §12-level; relocated soft-residue at §13.10 bullet 4" + the principle refinement framing
- the-stoa SPECIFICATION.md §12 (structural-fix author scope) + §13.10 bullet 4 (NC8 known-residue marker)
- operating-disciplines.md §27 (mechanical-script / agent-inspection split — the precedent the original framing cited)
- stoa--ojz / Arc 38 C1 — CAPTAIN_TIRO (the next structural-fix arc that would accrete data on the refined principle)
- stoa--myd — multi-checker convergence framing (deferred-with-gating; sibling N=1 substrate-canon-accretion ticket)

[from: user-tier-polybius] Arc 38 N-evidence accretion — two data points.

**Data point 1 — Trailer-preservation discipline (Arc 37 → Arc 38)**: The structural fix (omit `gh pr merge --body` to let GitHub auto-populate from source commits per stoa--6wp) worked first try this arc. Five §28 Co-Authored-By trailers preserved on squash-merge 0b5f7f3 (2× DAEDALUS_the-stoa + 2× ADA_the-stoa + Claude Opus 4.7). One confirming instance for the refined-principle thesis: "structural fixes narrow drift surface but require propagation discipline + iteration."

**Data point 2 — User-tier multi-substrate provenance opacity**: Post-Arc-38 `bash substrate/install.sh --target user` + `bash check.sh --workspace ~/.claude` returned: 0 drifted, 0 missing, **16 obsolete**. Inspection of the 16 obsolete entries confirms most are legitimate cross-substrate installs (agent-gauntlet plugin skills + earlier the-stoa generations + manual additions): arc-management, cite-check, format-validate, save-verdict, runner, dispatch-lieutenant, pulse-review, team-status, tier2-*, etc. — all enumerated in PRINCIPAL's current `Skill` tool surface as active.

The install.sh's own warning text correctly anticipates this ("at user-tier the destination may contain files from other substrates... this script cannot distinguish a substrate-rename leftover from a deliberate cross-substrate install"). The conservative default (enumerate, don't prune) is exactly the right behavior; bj5's `--prune-obsolete` flag stays gated behind explicit operator review.

This is N=2 confirming evidence that §29 multi-team interop is the right structural framing at the user-tier: substrate canon at any single workspace cannot reason cleanly about cross-installed provenance without explicit per-substrate provenance tracking. The Arc 38 manifest tracks the-stoa-specific files only (correct scope), but the resulting "obsolete" category sweeps in cross-substrate installs as a false-positive class that operator must manually triage.

Implication for future arcs: a per-substrate-origin marker on each deployed file (e.g., `# substrate-origin=the-stoa` in skill SKILL.md frontmatter) would let check.sh filter "obsolete" to only those files claiming the-stoa as origin. Out of Arc 38 scope (A20 hard-lock); flagging here as a potential next-cycle structural fix in the same family.

**Refined principle status (N=4 → N=5/6)**: One more arc of evidence that structural fixes are real but require iteration discipline to fully close. The trailer-discipline arc closed clean first try (Arc 37 → Arc 38, one cycle). The user-tier multi-substrate provenance gap remains structurally open (operator must manually distinguish cross-substrate installs from substrate-renamed leftovers). Same family, different propagation surface.
